formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: After the signature is submitted, the owner's USDS allowance for the spender is set to exactly `value`; any earlier allowance for that spender is replaced (Usds.permit: allowance[owner][spender] = value).
A value of type(uint256).max gives an allowance that is never reduced when the spender uses it (Usds.transferFrom and burn skip the decrease when allowed == max).
The spender can then move up to `value` USDS from the owner with transferFrom, or burn it with burn(from, value).
The signature can be used only until `deadline` (require(block.timestamp <= deadline)), and only once, because it uses up the owner's nonce.
formats.shown: The intent is 'Authorize spending of tokens'. Fields show the spender as a raw address, the maximum amount in USDS ('Unlimited' at 2^255 or more), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit test covers only a finite amount, not the 'Unlimited' threshold that the code treats as infinite allowance
findings.evidence: cases/0.json value '1500000000000000000000' renders '1500 USDS'. The descriptor's value field has threshold 0x8000… with message 'Unlimited'. Usds.sol transferFrom: if (allowed != type(uint256).max) { ... allowance decreases }.
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = 2^256-1 so the 'Unlimited' rendering is tested.
